seoTitle: Can You Put a Neon Sign Outside? IP Ratings & Weatherproof Guide
seoDescription: Can you put an LED neon sign outside or in the rain? IP65 vs IP67 waterproofing, outdoor power supplies, UV protection, and mounting safety explained.
summary: Yes, you can put an LED neon sign outside, but only if it is explicitly engineered with an IP65 or IP67 weatherproof build. Standard indoor neon signs will quickly corrode and fail if exposed to rain, humidity, or sunlight. A true outdoor build features sealed silicone flex, waterproof solder connections, a weatherproof IP67 power driver, and a GFCI-protected exterior circuit.
secondaryKeywords: can you put a neon sign outside
can neon signs be used outside
can led neon signs go outside
keyTakeaways: Standard indoor LED neon signs lack moisture barriers and will rapidly short-circuit, corrode copper solder joints, and yellow under UV sunlight if installed outdoors.
For covered outdoor environments like porches, awnings, and sheltered garden patios, an IP65 rating provides reliable protection against airborne humidity, splashback, and light moisture.
For direct exposure to driving rain, snow, or high-humidity coastal air, a full IP67 build with waterproof dielectric silicone injection potting is strictly necessary.
The primary failure point of outdoor illuminated signs is the power supply: never place an indoor transformer outdoors, and always use an IP67 aluminum driver with a cable drip loop.
Exterior mounting requires UV-stabilized cast acrylic backing with stainless steel standoff spacers to prevent moisture entrapment between the sign and the masonry wall.
